s01-title: Video eleven: Keycloak. One identity, roles per tenant, permissions per DocType.
s02-login: Desk signs in with Authorization Code and PKCE, right in the browser. The password is typed only into Keycloak; Astra gets back an authorization code and never sees the password.
s03-token: Roles are Keycloak groups: tenants, tenant name, role. Tuan is in saigon express sales. The tenant header only picks the tenant; permissions come from the signed token.
s04-me: Permissions are declared per DocType in YAML. Tuan can read, create and submit orders, not cancel. Desk reads the effective permissions from the I A M me API.
s05-desk: On Desk, permissions decide which buttons appear. Tuan's order has Save and Submit; a submitted order has no Cancel button. Someone else's order cannot be saved, but sales can still submit it, exactly as the YAML says.
s06-api: One order, four roles. Tuan, sales, cannot edit the waybill or cancel. Quang, ops, edits the waybill but cannot create orders. Ha, care, opens a ticket. Khoa, accounting, cancels. The kernel checks, so the API blocks too.
s07-sod: Segregation of duties: the maker cannot approve. Khoa's COD payment voucher, three hundred fifty thousand dong: his own Submit is refused. Thu, a second accountant, submits it, and the ledger posts at once. Desk and API both get four oh three.
s08-honest: To be accurate: row-level conditions are still on the roadmap. SAML and SCIM now run, in video 21.
s99-recap: Recap: Keycloak with PKCE, tenant roles read from the token, permissions declared on the DocType, and no self-approval. Next: the ledger.
s10-outro: Astra. One platform, every business process. Open source, MIT license.
